messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidics Platform for Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification Detection (DMF-LAMP)

REAGENTS USED:
  - LAMPMix (LAMP reaction reagents: 0.8 uM each inner primer FIP and BIP, 0.2 uM each outer primer FP and BP, 0.4 mM dNTP mix, 1 M betaine, 4 mM MgCl2, 1x supplied buffer, 8 U Bst DNA polymerase large fragment)
  - DNASample (target c-Myc proto-oncogene DNA resuspended in 1x enzyme buffer at 0.5 ng/uL, 0.14 uL droplets)

STEPS:
1. Dispense 10 droplets (~0.14 uL each, ~1.40 uL total) of LAMPMix from the left reservoir and transport to the central reaction reservoir via zig-zag electrodes.
2. Dispense 1 droplet (~0.14 uL) of DNASample from the right reservoir and transport to the central reaction reservoir.
3. Merge and mix the LAMP reagents and DNA sample droplets in the central reaction reservoir (total on-chip reaction volume: 1.54 uL, giving a final 0.5 ng/uL DNA concentration).
4. Incubate the reaction droplet isothermally at 65 C for 15 min (bottom-plate temperature set point; temperature gradient across droplet: 0.3 C).
5. Check amplification (fluorescence readout, standing in for gel-electrophoresis band intensity).
6. If no amplification detected, continue incubation at 65 C for a further 15 min (cumulative 30 min).
7. Check amplification again.
8. If still no amplification detected, continue incubation at 65 C for a further 15 min (cumulative 45 min).
9. Check amplification again. If still negative, discard reaction.
10. On successful amplification, transport the reaction product droplet to the retrieving reservoir and withdraw from the device via pipette.

INTERPRETATION: Successful c-Myc LAMP amplification is confirmed by the appearance of a characteristic LAMP ladder band pattern on gel electrophoresis (Figure 3e, Lane 7, positive at 45 min). The DMF-LAMP on-chip product shows higher normalized band fluorescence intensity (139.0 a.u.) than the equivalent bench-top reaction (78.8 a.u.), indicating enhanced amplification efficiency in the miniaturized DMF format. Negative controls show no amplification at any time point.

sources.title: A Digital Microfluidics Platform for Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification Detection

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the paper's on-chip DMF-LAMP protocol (Section 2.6 and Figure 1b/3e), covering the reagent dispensing and transport from opposing reservoirs (steps 1-2), merging and mixing in the central reaction reservoir (step 3), isothermal incubation at 65 C evaluated at 15-min checkpoints (steps 4-9), and product withdrawal (step 10). Reaction volumes (10 LAMP-mix droplets of 0.14 uL each + 1 DNA droplet of 0.14 uL = 1.54 uL total), DNA concentration (0.5 ng/uL), temperature (65 C bottom-plate set point), and time checkpoints (15, 30, 45 min, per Figure 3e) are taken directly from Sections 2.5-2.6. Because BioScript has no primitive for a persistent solid substrate or electrode actuation pattern, the zig-zag electrode transport and on-chip mixing motions are folded into the dispense and mix operations respectively. The DBS punch re-dispense pattern used in other protocols is not applicable here; LAMPMix and DNASample are each dispensed once. The detection modality in the paper is gel electrophoresis (band fluorescence intensity), not a fluorogenic real-time readout; 'detect fluorescence' is used as the BioScript stand-in for the generic amplification-confirmed readout, with the threshold (<=80 a.u.) representing absence of a positive LAMP band, consistent with the normalized intensities reported in Section 3.4 (139.0 a.u. positive vs. 78.8 a.u. bench-top). LAMP is isothermal and requires no thermal cycling; the repeat structure used in PCR protocols is intentionally absent. The bench-top LAMP optimization (Section 2.3-2.4), temperature gradient characterization (Section 3.2), impedance-based droplet velocity monitoring (Figure 3a-b), and bench-top comparison reactions (Figure 3f) are hardware-control or validation sub-experiments not captured in the core protocol translation.

numeric_mismatches.note: Detection in the paper is gel electrophoresis band fluorescence intensity. The threshold of 80 a.u. is derived from the bench-top positive control band intensity (78.8 a.u.) reported in Section 3.4; values at or below this represent no amplification. BioScript's 'detect fluorescence' is used as the sole available detect primitive; it stands in for the gel-electrophoresis readout rather than a real-time fluorescence signal.

numeric_mismatches.field: zig-zag electrode actuation and circular mixing
numeric_mismatches.note: The paper describes zig-zag crenelated electrodes improving droplet transport (Section 2.1) and the mixing reservoir kept activated during LAMP (Section 3.4). BioScript has no spatial actuation primitive; these are folded into the dispense and mix operations with no positional detail.

The paper characterizes a 0.3 C vertical temperature gradient across the droplet at 65 C bottom-plate set point (Section 3.2). BioScript's heat primitive specifies only a single temperature; the gradient and PID controller are hardware-level details not expressible in the language.
